title: API fallback heuristics - operator journal (draft)
content:
Purpose
- Short, practical operator journal for common API failure modes we see in production: request timeouts, 429 / rate-limit flurries, degraded streaming (partial payloads / stalls), and elevated 5xx/4xx error rates.
- This is an on-call scratch doc: fast checks, fallback heuristics, and temporary mitigations. Not the canonical postmortem (that goes to Confluence).

Scope
- Applies to hosted API frontends (edge + regional proxies) and runtime-backed endpoints.
- Focus on measured quick mitigations to restore customer-visible success rate / streaming health, not long-term remediation.

Failure signatures (what to look for quickly)
- Timeouts: tail latency spikes (p95/p99) with normal QPS. Client errors often show as 504 / upstream timeout.
- 429 bursts: sudden uptick in 429 ratio > 1% over baseline or sustained 429 spike tied to a customer or IP range.
- Streaming degradation: low token throughput, many sessions dropping mid-stream, partial chunking, or ABI-level 'incomplete' markers.
- Elevated error rate: 5xx increase across routes or a single route that serves a model variant.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 mins)
1) Confirm alert and scope: which routes, which regions, which token types.
   - Dashboard: Redwood Console -> Per-route -> Last 15m.
   - Slack alert channel: #sre-alerts.
2) Identify blast radius: is it a single customer token, model, region, or global?
3) Check infra health: GPU node health, autoscaler events, and cloud provider status pages.
4) Check recent deploys / rollouts: is a canary or rollout in flight? (Console -> Rollouts).
5) If streaming: pull a live trace (trace-id) and try reproducing short stream from a dev token.

Diagnostics (useful commands and queries)
- List failing requests by route (last 15m): logs.query("status>=500 or status==504") -> group by route/customer
- Check upstream latency heatmap: metrics.api_upstream_latency.p99{route="/v1/completions"}
- k8s: kubectl get pods -n runtime -l route=<route> -o wide
- Runtime process checks: curl -s http://localhost:9090/healthz && curl -s http://localhost:9090/kvcache/stats
- Proxy layer: check envoy stats: curl localhost:19000/stats

Timeout-specific interventions
- Short-term: reduce max_seq_len and request timeout at proxy for affected route to shed long-running queries. Patch via route config with: max_request_time=30s (was 120s).
- Enable prefix-KV cache for hot prompts where applicable.
- If root cause is model-side slow tokens (token generation hot-spot), switch to a faster model variant (quantized or smaller) for affected route using the immediate fallback policy.
- If GPU starvation: check node dashboards and consider burst capacity from Dedicated pool (manual scale out).

429 / rate-limited flows (common patterns & mitigations)
- Signature: 429 spikes often correlate with client retry storms or sudden GRPC reconnect flows. Look for single customer or IP bursts.
- Contain: temporarily raise quota for affected enterprise customer only if agreed with CS, otherwise enforce a hard per-key throttle and notify CS.
- Smooth: apply token bucket smoothing at the proxy and enable small backoff_hint headers (Retry-After: 1).
- Quick triage: find offending key via logs, identify call pattern (batching vs loop), reach out to customer if needed.

Degraded streaming (partial frames / stalls)
- Symptoms: clients see long gaps between chunks, or closing of stream with HTTP 200 but 'incomplete' body.
- Quick check: examine websocket / chunked transfer metrics and per-connection send buffers.
- Short fix: switch route to non-streaming/response-chunked mode for heavy endpoints temporarily (fall back to aggregated responses).
- Try toggling streaming buffer size and enabling per-connection limit on concurrent streams.
- If caused by proxy Egress throttling -> route to different egress region or increase egress burst window.

Elevated error rate (5xx / 4xx rise)
- Determine pattern: are errors auth/validation (4xx) or backend (5xx)?
- For 5xx across many routes: likely infra (db, metric store, runtime crash). Pull node crash logs and OOM traces.
- For a single model variant: rollback to prior model version (Console -> Rollouts -> rollback).
- If database or metadata store is slow: enable degraded mode that serves from cache for read-only endpoints.

Fallback matrix (quick decision guide)
- Single customer spike -> throttle / quota bump (customer-facing) -> contact CS.
- Single model variant causing high latency/errors -> route to previous model version or smaller quantized variant.
- Region-local infra issue -> traffic-shift to secondary region (smart routing policy).
- Global overload -> enable global degradation profile: reduce token budgets, enable response summarization, increase sampling for streaming.

Communications & runbook steps for pager responders
- 0-10m: Confirm alert, scope, and mitigation plan. Post to incident thread with short summary and who is owning.
- 10-30m: Apply safe mitigations (throttles, model fallback, traffic-shift). Update incident thread with ETA to restore.
- 30-90m: Stabilize, monitor, and escalate to infra/product owners if rollback or capacity purchase needed.
- After stable: kick off a post-incident ticket with timeline and immediate root cause hypotheses.

Escalation contacts (quick)
- SRE lead: Miguel Torres (pager)
- Serving runtime owner: Hannah Li
- Product owner (hosted API): Omar Rahman
- Customer Success (for customer-impactful throttles): Priya Menon

SLO thresholds to compare against (quick reference)
- p95 latency target: 300ms
- p99 latency target: 1200ms
- error budget burn: >5% in 1h -> high-priority incident
- streaming success rate target: 99.5% (1h window)

Notes to self / TODOs (non-blocking while oncall)
- Add automatic traffic-shift play for region failover (Console runbook).
- Create per-customer backoff hints that include a friendly error message and suggested client retry strategy.
- Improve correlated tracing between proxy and runtime for streaming traces.
- Experiment: soft-serve fallback that downgrades generation params (nucleus->top-k) to reduce token generation time.

Post-incident template for quick autopsy (fill in during follow-up)
- Incident start: [time]
- End: [time]
- Signal that triggered pager: [metric/alert]
- Blast radius: [routes/customers/regions]
- Immediate mitigation(s) applied: [throttles/rollbacks/traffic-shift]
- Root cause hypothesis: [short]
- Remediation action items: [list, owners, ETA]
- Lessons learned: [bullet points]

Appendix: sample quick commands
- Find top erroring keys: logs.query("status>=500") | top_by("api_key", 20)
- Force rollback to previous model: curl -X POST $CONSOLE_API/rollouts/rollback -d '{"route":"/v1/completions"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
- Enable per-route throttle: curl -X PATCH $CONSOLE_API/routes/<route> -d '{"rate_limit":{"requests_per_minute":500}}'

Endnotes / small notes
- This doc is intentionally terse. Keep it in sync with the canonical SRE runbook on Confluence but feel free to jot quick observations here.
- If you add an action that might impact SLAs (quota changes / rollback) call out CS and Legal if it's an enterprise customer.

Patch log (journal)
- 2024-08-15 A.Patel created initial sketch after recurring streaming incident.
- 2024-09-04 M.Torres added 429 heuristics and customer throttle guidance.
- 2024-11-02 H.Li added fallback matrix and post-incident template.
